365842.title: Gray-code canonical coloring conjecture for powers of paths

full_record.title: Gray-code canonical coloring conjecture for powers of paths
full_record.statement:

365923.title: Dimension bound and equality characterization for binary graphical descriptions

full_record.title: Dimension bound and equality characterization for binary graphical descriptions
full_record.statement:
Fix a tuple of graphs $(\mathcal{G}_1,\dots,\mathcal{G}_d)$ on vertex set $[r]$, and let $W \subset (\mathbb{R}^2)^{\otimes d}$ be the set described by this tuple. Assume that the tuple is a valid graphical description, so each $\mathcal{G}_j$ is a disjoint union of $c_j$ complete bipartite graphs. **Graphical-description dimension conjecture.** Then

$$
r+\sum_{j=1}^d c_j\leq 2^{d-1}+d,
$$

with equality only if $r=2^{d-1}$. This proposed bound would constrain the expected dimensions of all valid graphical-description varieties and would identify the only possible equality value of the number of summands.

367998.title: Bhanja–Kom–Pandey lower-bound and inverse conjecture for positive restricted signed sumsets

full_record.title: Bhanja–Kom–Pandey lower-bound and inverse conjecture for positive restricted signed sumsets
full_record.statement:
Let $A$ be a set of $k\geq 4$ positive integers, and let $h$ be an integer with $3\leq h\leq k-1$. The restricted signed $h$-fold sumset is denoted by $h^{\wedge}_{\pm}A$. **Bhanja–Kom–Pandey's conjecture.** One should have

$$
\left|h^{\wedge}_{\pm}A\right|\geq 2hk-h^2+1.
$$

This lower bound is best possible. Moreover, if equality holds, then

$$
A=d\ast\{1,3,\ldots,2k-1\}
$$

for some positive integer $d$. The conjecture gives the expected lower bound and equality case for positive-integer restricted signed sumsets; the source states that the case $h=3$ was proved, while the general range remains conjectural.

359174.title: The polynomial noncrossing-path conjecture

full_record.title: The polynomial noncrossing-path conjecture
full_record.statement: A **complete $n$-vertex simple topological graph** is a drawing of the complete graph on $n$ vertices in which vertices are points and edges are simple curves, with no edge passing through a nonincident vertex and with any two edges meeting at most once. 360715.title: The multiplicative bounded-product conjecture

full_record.title: The multiplicative bounded-product conjecture
full_record.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ have positive density with respect to a multiplicative Følner sequence. For an infinite set $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and $t\in\mathbb{N}$, consider

$$

**Multiplicative bounded-product conjecture.** There exist an infinite set $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and $t\in\mathbb{N}$ such that

$$
\{b_1b_2t:b_1,b_2\in B,\ b_1\ne b_2\}\subset A.
$$

361097.title: The sparse r-chromatic graph triangle conjecture

full_record.title: The sparse r-chromatic graph triangle conjecture
full_record.statement:
A graph $G$ is **$r$-chromatic** if its chromatic number satisfies $\chi(G)\geq r$, and let $t(G)$ denote its number of triangles. Here $e(G)$ denotes the number of edges of $G$.

**Sparse r-chromatic graph triangle conjecture.** There exists $c>0$ such that every $r$-chromatic graph with at most

$$
cr^3\log^2 r
$$

edges contains at least

$$
\binom r3

370646.title: Stability conjecture for nontrivial direct product graph pairs

full_record.title: Stability conjecture for nontrivial direct product graph pairs
full_record.statement:
A graph pair $(\Gamma,\Sigma)$ is **nontrivial** if $\Gamma$ and $\Sigma$ are coprime connected twin-free graphs and exactly one of them is bipartite. A graph pair is **stable** if it has no unexpected automorphisms under the direct product construction. **Stability conjecture.** Let $(\Gamma,\Sigma)$ be a nontrivial graph pair with $\Sigma$ bipartite. Then $(\Gamma,\Sigma)$ is stable if and only if $\Gamma$ is stable.

The conjecture would eliminate the need for any additional condition in the reduction of stability for a nontrivial pair with bipartite second factor to stability of the single graph $\Gamma$. Explicitly determining stable nontrivial pairs is difficult, even when $\Sigma=K_2$, so the conjecture represents a broad proposed reduction of the stability problem.
full_record.source_name: Xiaomeng Wang, Yan-Li Qin and Binzhou Xia, “The existence of unexpected automorphisms in direct product graphs”, arXiv:2509.26170 (2026).

full_record.statement:
Let $KG_n$ be the Knödel graph on even $n$ vertices, and let $\gamma(KG_n)$ denote its domination number. Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $k\geq2$ be an integer. $$
\gamma(KG_n)\leq\left\lceil\frac{2n}{p^k}\right\rceil.

350249.title: Weaker type-2 growth conjecture for the cryptographic tensor-product space

full_record.title: Weaker type-2 growth conjecture for the cryptographic tensor-product space
full_record.statement:
Let $n$, $k$, and $\tilde k'$ be the parameters in the construction, let $\mathcal{S}_1^{\tilde k'\!, n}$ denote the corresponding trace-class space, and let $\ell_2^{k\tilde k'}$ be Euclidean space. For the restricted type-2 constant $\mathrm{T}_2^{(m)}$ and logarithmic comparison $\lesssim_{\log}$ used in the paper, define

$$
X=\left(\mathcal{S}_1^{\tilde k'\!, n}\otimes_{(\varepsilon,\pi)_{1/2}}\mathcal{S}_1^{\tilde k'\!, n}\right)\otimes_\varepsilon\ell_2^{k\tilde k'}.
$$

**Weaker-form conjecture.** There exists a dimension-independent constant $\beta<1$ such that

$$
\mathrm{T}_2^{(n^2)}(X)\lesssim_{\log}n^\beta.
$$

This weaker estimate would still imply the desired bounds for position-based cryptography. The source gives no evidence that the conjecture has been resolved.

350796.title: Vince–Wang's minimum-density conjecture for graphs of minimum degree three

full_record.title: Vince–Wang's minimum-density conjecture for graphs of minimum degree three
full_record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected finite simple graph with vertex set of order $n$, and let $\mathcal C(G)$ be the collection of its nonempty connected vertex sets. Define

$$
A(G)=\frac{1}{|\mathcal C(G)|}\sum_{U\in\mathcal C(G)}|U|,
$$

and define the density of connected sets by

$$
D(G)=\frac{A(G)}{n}.
$$

**Vince–Wang's conjecture.** If $G$ is a connected graph all of whose vertices have degree at least $3$, then

$$
D(G)\geq\frac12.
$$

For trees, Vince and Wang proved the corresponding lower bound, while the extension to general connected graphs remains open; the paper establishes only a lower bound close to $1/2$ for highly connected graphs.

381594.title: The unrestricted cylindrical width conjecture for finite transitive subsets of complex spheres

full_record.title: The unrestricted cylindrical width conjecture for finite transitive subsets of complex spheres
full_record.statement:
Let $1\le k\le d$. Let $X$ be a finite transitive subset of the unit sphere in $\mathbb{C}^d$. **Unrestricted cylindrical width conjecture.** There is a complex $k$-dimensional subspace $W$ such that

$$
\sup_{\mathbf{x}\in X}\lVert\operatorname{proj}_W\mathbf{x}\rVert_2 \lesssim \frac{1}{\sqrt{\log(2d/k)}}.
$$

The preceding theorem proves this estimate under the additional restriction $k\le d/(\log(3d))^C$; the authors suspect that this restriction is unnecessary, so the conjecture concerns all $1\le k\le d$.

345114.title: Satisfying sequences for rainbow matchings in multipartite hypergraphs

full_record.title: Satisfying sequences for rainbow matchings in multipartite hypergraphs
full_record.statement:
Let $n\geq s$ and let $k$ be a positive integer. A nondecreasing sequence $f_1\leq\cdots\leq f_s$ is called **satisfying** if every collection of families $\mathcal F_1,\ldots,\mathcal F_s\subset [n]^k$ with $|\mathcal F_i|>f_i$ contains a rainbow matching, meaning a choice of pairwise disjoint tuples $F_i\in\mathcal F_i$. **Satisfying-sequence conjecture.** The sequences $d_1,\ldots,d_s$ and $e_1,\ldots,e_s$ defined by

$$
d_i:=\min(i+C\sqrt{s\log s},s-1)n^{k-1},\qquad e_i:=i\cdot n^{k-1}
$$

are satisfying. The paper presents these sequences in its discussion of the separate-threshold problem; the surrounding text gives supporting results for related sequences, while the exact asserted status of these sequences is not resolved in the supplied context.

360603.title: Brakensiek–Guruswami's approximate graph homomorphism hardness conjecture
360603.literal_statement:
Let $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ be non-bipartite loopless undirected graphs such that $\mathbf{A}\to\mathbf{B}$. The **Brakensiek–Guruswami conjecture** asserts that

$$
\operatorname{PCSP}(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B})
$$

is $\operatorname{NP}$-hard. Here $\operatorname{PCSP}(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{B})$ is the approximate graph homomorphism problem distinguishing instances homomorphic to $\mathbf{A}$ from instances not homomorphic to $\mathbf{B}$. This is presented as a stronger conjecture than the approximate graph-colouring conjecture; the source identifies graphs with loops or bipartite graphs as trivial or reducible to $2$-colouring, while the stated non-bipartite loopless case remains open.

360610.title: Speyer's conjecture on matroid subdivision face numbers
360610.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a subdivision of $\Delta_{k,n}$ into smaller matroid polytopes. For each $1\leq i\leq n$, let $f_i$ be the number of cells of $\mathcal{S}$ of dimension $n-i$ lying in the interior of $\Delta_{k,n}$. **Speyer's conjecture.** One has

$$
f_i \leq \binom{n-1-i}{k-i}\binom{n-k-1}{i-1}.
$$

Moreover, simultaneous equality holds if and only if all facets of $\mathcal{S}$ correspond to base polytopes of series-parallel matroids. This conjecture predicts sharp bounds on the face numbers of matroid subdivisions of the hypersimplex; its resolution status is not specified in the source.

360612.title: Positivity conjecture for connected matroids with series-parallel subdivisions
360612.literal_statement:
Let $\mathsf{M}$ be a connected matroid whose base polytope admits a subdivision into direct sums of series-parallel matroids, and define

$$
\wwtilde{g}_{\mathsf{M}}(t):=\frac{1}{t}g_{\mathsf{M}}(t).
$$

**Connected series-parallel subdivision conjecture.** The polynomial $\wwtilde{g}_{\mathsf{M}}(t-1)$ has non-negative coefficients. This is a stronger positivity statement beyond Schubert matroids and is accompanied in the source by the open challenge of characterizing all matroids admitting such subdivisions; no resolution status is supplied.

360713.title: The ordered two-set sumset conjecture in the primes
360713.literal_statement:
Let $\mathcal P$ denote the primes. Seek infinite sets $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and $C\subset\mathcal P-1$ such that

$$
\{b+c:b\in B,\ c\in C,\ b<c\}\subset\mathcal P.
$$

**Ordered prime sumset conjecture.** There exist such infinite sets $B$ and $C$.
The source presents this as an explicitly open ordered analogue of the prime bounded finite-sums conjecture, following the known ordered sumset result with unrestricted infinite sets.

360739.title: Conjecture on zero-dimensionality of the walk-generating-function polynomial system
360739.literal_statement:
Let $K$ be the field of algebraic functions over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $P$ denote the polynomial system defined in the paper's theorem on the $S$-regular tree. The ideal generated by $P$ is the ideal generated by all polynomials in that system.

**Zero-dimensionality conjecture.** The ideal generated by $P$ is zero dimensional.

If true, this would imply that the $T$-weighted closed-walk generating functions are algebraic and that each generating function admits a bivariate polynomial relation arising from a Gröbner basis. The paper presents this as supported by empirical evidence; no resolution is supplied.

360771.title: Composition-partition invariance conjecture for Dyck graphs
360771.literal_statement:
Let $G=([n],E)$ be a Dyck graph. For a composition $\alpha\vDash n$, let $\lambda(\alpha)$ be the partition obtained by rearranging its parts, and let $\mathcal{N}_{G,\alpha}$ be the associated set of permutations. **Composition-partition invariance conjecture.**

$$
\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{N}_{G,\alpha}}q^{\widetilde{\mathsf{inv}}_G(\sigma)}=\sum_{\sigma \in \mathcal{N}_{G,\lambda(\alpha)}}q^{\widetilde{\mathsf{inv}}_G(\sigma)}.
$$

The paper presents this as equivalent to the preceding Psi-expansion conjecture using the known power-sum formula for Dyck graphs.

360772.title: Psi-expansion conjecture for interval-graph permutation functions
360772.literal_statement:
Let $G=([n],E)$ be an interval graph and let $\tau\in\mathfrak{S}_n$. Let $\Phi_G(\tau)$, $\mathcal{Q}_{\Phi_G(\tau)}^{(G)}$, $\mathsf{CoInv}_G$, and $\mathsf{Inv}_G$ be the functions and statistics defined in the paper; let $\mathcal{N}_{G,\alpha}$ and $z_\alpha$ be as above, and let $\omega$ be the involution on $\operatorname{QSym}$. **General Psi-expansion conjecture.**

$$
\omega \mathcal{Q}_{\Phi_G(\tau)}^{(G)}=\sum_{\alpha\vDash n}\frac{\Psi_\alpha}{z_{\alpha}}\#\{\sigma\in\mathcal{N}_{G,\alpha}\mid\mathsf{CoInv}_G(\sigma^{-1})=\mathsf{Inv}_G(\tau)\}.
$$

This generalizes the preceding interval-graph expansion and relates the involuted quasisymmetric function to permutation statistics.

360955.title: The unimodality conjecture for plucking polynomials of hedgehog rooted trees
360955.literal_statement: Let $T=T_{1,1,\ldots,1}$ be the **hedgehog rooted tree** (or star rooted tree) with $n$ rays, and let $f$ be a delay function whose values are $1$ or $2$. The plucking polynomial with delay function is denoted by $Q(T,f)$. **Unimodality conjecture.** The polynomial $Q(T,f)$ is unimodal. The plucking polynomial is of particular interest because of its connections to knot theory via the Kauffman bracket skein relations. Experimental calculations suggest this unimodality for delay functions with values $1$ or $2$, while examples with other delay functions are not always unimodal; the conjecture remains open.

361155.title: The wreath conjecture for decompositions of uniform subsets
361155.literal_statement: Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let a **wreath** be the collection of intervals obtained from a cyclic permutation of $[n]$ by choosing a $k$-element interval and then successively choosing the interval starting immediately after the end of the preceding one, continuing until the initial interval is reached. Thus a wreath contains $\operatorname{lcm}(n,k)/k$ intervals and goes around the cycle $\operatorname{lcm}(n,k)/n$ times. **The wreath conjecture.** The family of all $k$-element subsets of $[n]$ can be decomposed into disjoint wreaths. This is an old and difficult problem related to the Baranyai theorem; the source mentions related earlier results and open problems, but does not indicate a resolution of this conjecture.

361234.title: Bandari–Herzog's conjecture on componentwise polymatroidal ideals
361234.literal_statement: Let $S=K[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be a polynomial ring over a field $K$. A monomial ideal $I\subset S$ is **componentwise polymatroidal** when each component $I_{\langle j\rangle}$ is polymatroidal, where $I_{\langle j\rangle}$ is generated by the degree-$j$ monomials belonging to $I$. **Bandari–Herzog's conjecture.** If $I$ is componentwise polymatroidal, then $I$ has linear quotients. Since polymatroidal ideals have linear quotients, this is a particular case of Jahan–Zheng's conjecture; the source presents it as the conjecture proved positively by the paper.

361270.title: Casselgren–Petrosyan conjecture for outerplanar graphs

361272.title: The friendship paradox inequality for Binomial, Geometric and Poisson variables
361272.literal_statement:
Let $(X_i)_{i\begin{smallmatrix}\[-0.6em]{}
\end{smallmatrix}\in\fac-?}$ be i.i.d. random variables, each having a Binomial, Geometric or Poisson distribution, defined on a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb P)$. Then

**The friendship paradox inequality.**

$$
\mathbb P\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{X_0}X_i\geq X_0(X_0-1)\right\}\geq \frac{1}{2},
$$

where the empty sum is equal to zero.

This inequality would establish significance of the friendship paradox for the corresponding random-variable models and motivates the graph results studied in the paper. The source presents it as a conjecture, and no resolution is given.

361308.title: The Fine-number enumeration conjecture for valleyless-tieless parking functions
361308.literal_statement:
A **valleyless-tieless parking function** of length $n$ is a parking function $(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$ with no index $1\leq i\leq n-1$ such that $a_i=a_{i+1}$ and no index $2\leq i\leq n-1$ such that $a_{i-1}>a_i<a_{i+1}$. Let ${\mathrm{VTPF}}_n$ denote the set of valleyless-tieless parking functions of length $n$, and let $F_i$ be the $i$th Fine number. **Fine-number enumeration conjecture.** Valleyless-tieless parking functions of length $n$ are enumerated by

$$
|{\mathrm{VTPF}}_n|=F_{n-3}.
$$

This is presented as an open problem in the paper; the statement includes the indexing convention for the Fine numbers but gives no evidence of a resolution.

369795.title: Davydov–Marcugini–Pambianco orbit-count conjecture for generic lines in $PG(3,q)$
369795.literal_statement: Let $q$ be a power of $3$, let $G=PGL_2(q)$ act on the lines of $PG(3,q)$, and let $C$ be the twisted cubic. A line is **generic** if it neither intersects $C$ nor lies in any osculating plane of $C$; write $\mathcal{O}_6$ for the class of generic lines. **Davydov–Marcugini–Pambianco's conjecture.** The number of $G$-orbits of generic lines of $PG(3,q)$ is $2q-3$, of which there are $q/3$, $q-1$, and $(2q-6)/3$ orbits of sizes $|G|$, $|G|/2$, and $|G|/4$, respectively. This conjecture gives the proposed classification of the generic-line class $\mathcal{O}_6$ into $G$-orbits in characteristic $3$, a case that had remained open after the corresponding problems in characteristics different from $2$ and $3$, and in characteristic $2$, were solved.

382076.title: Ma–Zha–She coset equation conjecture
382076.literal_statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $H=\langle-1,2\rangle\subset\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$, let $\ell_0$ be the index parameter used for $H$, and let $g$ be a generator of $\mathbb{F}_p^{\times}$. **Ma–Zha–She conjecture.** If $\ell_0\geq 3$, then there exist $b\in gH$ and $c\in g^2H$ such that

$$
1+b+c=0
$$

in $\mathbb{F}_p$. The conjecture gives the coset triples needed for the preceding construction and, unlike the preceding formulation, does not assume $4\nmid o_p(2)$.

372011.title: Reduced TAS-tree conjecture for trees without isomorphic pairs
372011.literal_statement:
An **undirected tree** is a connected graph with no cycles. A **caterpillar** is a tree for which removing all leaves results in a path. An **isomorphic pair** in a graph consists of disjoint vertex sets inducing isomorphic subgraphs and satisfying the specified two-edge cut condition. An orientation has the **tournament anti-Sidorenko property** (TAS) when it satisfies the tournament anti-Sidorenko inequality.

**Reduced TAS-tree conjecture.** For every undirected tree that is not a caterpillar, has at least $2$ vertices of even degree, and has no isomorphic pair, there exists some orientation that has the tournament anti-Sidorenko property.

Caterpillars and trees reducible by isomorphic-pair pruning are already covered by results in the paper, so this conjecture is the remaining reduced case of the TAS-tree problem.

360710.title: The uniform sets bounded-sums conjecture
360710.literal_statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$ and $k\geq2$. Let $\Phi=(\Phi_N)_{N\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a Følner sequence. A set is $\mathsf{U}^k(\Phi)$-uniform when its indicator has correlations along $\Phi$, positive density along $\Phi$, and vanishing $\mathsf{U}^k(\Phi)$ seminorm after subtracting its density. For an infinite $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ and $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$, write

$$
B^{\oplus\ell}=\left\{\sum_{n\in F}n:F\subset B,\ |F|=\ell\right\}.
$$

$$

374571.title: Erdős–Kleitman matching conjecture for set families
374571.literal_statement:
Let $e(n,s)$ denote the maximum size of a family $\mathcal{F}\subset 2^{[n]}$ with matching number $\nu(\mathcal{F})<s$. For $1\leq i\leq k$, let

$$
\mathcal{A}_i^{(k)}(n,s)=\Bigl\{F\in {[n]\choose k}:|F\cap [si-1]|\ge i\Bigr\}.
$$

Let $\mathcal{P}(m,s,\ell)$ be the family defined for $n=sm+s-\ell$ by

$$
\mathcal{P}(m,s,\ell)=\bigl\{P\subset [n]: |P|+|P\cap [\ell-1]|\ge m+1\bigr\}.
$$

**Erdős–Kleitman matching conjecture.** Suppose that $s\ge 2$, $m\ge 1$, and $n=sm+s-\ell$ for some integer $0<\ell\leq\lceil s/2\rceil$. Then

$$
e(sm+s-\ell,s)=|\mathcal{P}(m,s,\ell)|.
$$

The conjecture concerns the extremal size of set families avoiding an $s$-matching. It is known in several cases, including $\ell=2$, $m=1$, $s\geq \ell m+3\ell+3$, and $m=2$, while the general assertion remains open.
374571.ordinary_attempt_and_exact_gap: Source Conjecture 2 matches. Theorem 4 requires s sufficiently large depending on m and epsilon and ell≤(1/2−epsilon)s. It leaves small s and the central boundary ell=ceil(s/2); no choice of a fixed positive epsilon covers that boundary. Need full extremal upper bound; source known subcases and feasible family are not a solution.

376138.title: The strong Seymour vertex conjecture for oriented graphs
376138.literal_statement: Let $D$ be an oriented graph. For a vertex $x$, let $N_D^+(x)$ and $N_D^{++}(x)$ denote its out-neighborhood and second out-neighborhood, respectively. A **complete matching** from $X$ to $Y$ is a matching consisting of arcs directed from vertices of $X$ to vertices of $Y$ and having every vertex of $X$ as a tail. A vertex $x$ is a **strong Seymour vertex** if there is a complete matching from $N_D^+(x)$ to $N_D^{++}(x)$. **Strong Seymour vertex conjecture.** Every oriented graph contains a strong Seymour vertex. This would strengthen Seymour's second neighborhood conjecture, since a complete matching injects $N_D^+(x)$ into $N_D^{++}(x)$. 376117.title: Jackson–Thomassen conjecture on strong orientations of digraphs
376117.literal_statement:
Let $D=(V,A)$ be a digraph. It is **$k$-strong** if it has at least $k+1$ vertices and remains strongly connected after the deletion of any subset of $k-1$ vertices. An **oriented subdigraph** is obtained by retaining exactly one arc from every directed $2$-cycle of $D$.

376358.title: Linear Erdős–Pósa bound for models of forests
376358.literal_statement:
Let $F$ be a forest and let $R \subseteq V(F)$. For a graph $G$, a set $S \subseteq V(G)$, and a positive integer $k$, consider models of $(F,R)$ in $(G,S)$.

**Linear Erdős–Pósa conjecture.** At least one of the following holds:

1. There are $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint models of $(F,R)$ in $(G,S)$.
2. There is a set $X \subseteq V(G)$ with

$$
|X| \leq |V(F)|(k-1)
$$

such that there is no model of $(F,R)$ in $(G-X,S \setminus X)$.

This would give a bound linear in the size of the forest, improving the dependence on $|V(T)|$ in the established Erdős–Pósa result for $S$-rooted models of a fixed tree. The conjecture is stated in the more general setting of $(F,R)$-models and is open in the supplied source.

367887.title: Elphick–Wocjan conjecture on the spectral lower bound for clique number
367887.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices, let $
\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n$ be the eigenvalues of its adjacency matrix, and let $
s^+$ be the sum of the squares of its positive eigenvalues:

$$
s^+ = \sum_{\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i^2.
$$

Let $\omega$ denote the clique number of $G$. **Elphick–Wocjan conjecture.** The positive-eigenvalue spectral quantity satisfies

$$
\sqrt{s^+} \leq n\left(1-\frac{1}{\omega}\right).
$$

Equivalently,

$$
\frac{n}{n-\sqrt{s^+}}\leq\omega.
$$

This conjecture strengthens Wilf's spectral lower bound on the clique number by replacing the largest adjacency eigenvalue with the square root of the sum of the squares of all positive eigenvalues. It is also stated as the second problem in a survey of open problems in spectral graph theory.

367966.title: Hill's crossing-number conjecture for complete graphs
367966.statement:
Let $K_n$ be the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\operatorname{cr}(K_n)$ denote its crossing number, the minimum number of crossings in a drawing of $K_n$ in the plane or sphere. Define

$$
X(n):=\frac{1}{4}\Big\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \Big\rfloor \Big\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2}\Big\rfloor.
$$

**Hill's conjecture.** The crossing number satisfies

$$
\operatorname{cr}(K_n)=X(n)=\frac{3}{8}\binom{n}{4}+O(n^3).
$$

This is a foundational unsolved problem in geometric graph theory. The conjecture was first studied by Hill in the 1950s, and the displayed quantity is attained by the standard conjectured optimal drawings; the equality is not known for general $n$.

368385.title: Freiman–Lev conjecture on restricted double sumsets
368385.statement:
Let $A=\{a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_{k-1}\}$ be a set of $k>7$ integers such that

$$
0=a_0<a_1<\cdots<a_{k-1}
$$

and let $d(A)=1$ denote that the greatest common divisor of all differences between elements of $A$ is $1$. Write $2^{\wedge}A$ for the restricted twofold sumset, consisting of sums of two distinct elements of $A$.

**Freiman–Lev conjecture.** One has

$$
\left|2^{\wedge}A\right|\geq
\begin{cases}
a_{k-1}+k-2, & a_{k-1}\leq 2k-5,\\
3k-7, & a_{k-1}\geq 2k-4.
\end{cases}
$$

This conjecture concerns the minimum possible size of a restricted double sumset in terms of the largest element of a normalized integer set. The source attributes it to Freiman and Lev; no resolution is supplied here.

368543.title: Conjecture that nontrivial snarks of high perfect matching index are strong
368543.statement:
Let $G$ be a nontrivial snark, and let its perfect matching index be the minimum number of perfect matchings covering all edges of $G$. An edge of a snark is **suppressible** if suppressing it preserves the relevant snark structure; the snark is **strong** when all its edges are suppressible.

**Strong-snark conjecture.** With the sole exception of the Petersen graph, every nontrivial snark with perfect matching index at least $5$ is strong; equivalently, all its edges are suppressible.

The conjecture is motivated by computations on thousands of nontrivial snarks, all of which were found to be strong. It does not extend to the paper's low-cyclic-connectivity examples, which have perfect matching index $5$ but contain non-removable edges, and its general status is open.

368599.title: Linear induced saturation conjecture for disjoint unions of chains
368599.statement:
Let $C_k$ denote the chain poset with $k$ elements, and let $\bigoplus_{j=1}^m C_{i_j}$ be the disjoint union of chains with $i_1\ge i_2\ge\dots\ge i_m$. For a poset $P$, write $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,P)$ for the minimum size of an induced $P$-saturated family in $2^{[n]}$. **Linear induced saturation conjecture.** For any $i_1\ge i_2\ge\dots\ge i_m$, there exists $C=C(i_1,i_2,\dots,i_m)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\bigoplus_{j=1}^m C_{i_j})\le C\cdot n.
$$

At the time of the paper, it was unknown whether any poset has superlinear induced saturation number. If true, this conjecture is best possible because $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,2C_2)=\Theta(n)$ is known.

368618.title: The strong $\delta$-conjecture for the Colin de Verdière parameter
368618.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Let $\delta(G)$ be its minimum degree, let $l(G)$ be its degeneracy,

$$
l(G)=\max\\{\delta(H):H\text{ is a subgraph of }G\\},

**Strong $\delta$-conjecture for $\nu$.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\delta(G)\leq l(G)\leq \lceil\delta\rceil(G)\leq \nu(G).
$$

The first two inequalities follow directly from the definitions, while the conjectural content is the final inequality. The source later says that the corresponding original $\delta$-conjecture is used conditionally and does not supply a resolution of this full chain in the candidate span.

367473.title: Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar's girth conjecture for Wenger-type graphs
367473.statement:
Let $D(k,q)$ be the graph defined by the parameters $k$ and the prime power $q$. **Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar's conjecture.** For every prime power $q\ge 4$, the graph has girth

$$
\operatorname{girth}(D(k,q))=
\begin{cases}
k+5, & k\text{ odd},\\
k+4, & k\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
$$

The source records matching lower bounds and presents equality as conjectural; no general resolution is supplied.

324165.title: A minor characterization of signed graphs with signed Colin de Verdière parameter at most three
324165.literal_statement:
A **signed graph** is a pair $(G,\Sigma)$ consisting of a graph $G$ and a set $\Sigma$ of odd edges. Let $\nu(G,\Sigma)$ denote its signed Colin de Verdière parameter. Write $K_5^o$ for the signed complete graph on five vertices with the specified odd-edge pattern, and $K_4^=$ for the corresponding signed complete graph on four vertices. A **$\Delta Y$-transformation** replaces a triangle by a new degree-three vertex adjacent to its vertices, and a **$Y\Delta$-transformation** is the reverse operation. 

**Minor characterization conjecture.** A signed graph $(G,\Sigma)$ has $\nu(G,\Sigma)\leq 3$ if and only if $(G,\Sigma)$ has no minor isomorphic to $K_5^o$, $K_4^=$, or any signed graph $(H,\Omega)$ that can be obtained from $K_4^=$ by a sequence of $\Delta Y$- and $Y\Delta$-transformations.

This conjecture seeks the next excluded-minor characterization for the signed Colin de Verdière parameter after the established characterization for parameter at most two. The paper notes that $\nu(K_5^o)=4$ and $\nu(K_4^=)=4$, and that the parameter remains four under the indicated transformations; the proposed characterization is otherwise unresolved in the supplied text.

326378.title: Indexed strong Goldbach representation conjecture
326378.literal_statement:
Distribute the positive integers into three columns $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$ by residue class modulo $3$, and let $t_n^\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^*$ denote the integer in column $C_n$ and row $\alpha$. Let $\mathbb{P}$ be the set of positive prime numbers, ordered as $p_1=2,p_2=3,p_3=5,\dots$, and let $p_m^\delta$ denote the prime in the $m$-th prime column and row $\delta$. For a positive even integer $t_n^\alpha$, the conjecture specifies a representation using one prime in the corresponding prime column and another prime.

**Indexed strong Goldbach representation conjecture.** Let $t_n^\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^*$ be a positive even integer. Then there esist two prime numbers $p_{n}^{\delta(\alpha)}, \,p_{m}^{\gamma}\in\mathbb{P}$ such that

$$
t_{n}^{\alpha}=p_{n}^{\delta(\alpha)}+p_{m}^{\gamma}.
$$

This is presented as a reformulation of the strong Goldbach conjecture in the paper's column-and-row notation. Its status therefore tracks the unresolved strong Goldbach problem rather than constituting an independent result.

332014.title: The weight-support system conjecture for perfect codes containing Preparata codes
332014.literal_statement:
Let $C$ be a binary perfect code containing a Preparata code. For an extended perfect code, consider the codewords of weight $4$; for a non-extended perfect code, consider the codewords of weight $3$. Their supports form the corresponding Steiner system. A system is **linear** when it is equivalent to the system formed by the supports of the weight-$3$ words of the linear Hamming code.

**Weight-support system conjecture.** All codewords of weight $3$ of a perfect code containing a Preparata code, and all codewords of weight $4$ of an extended perfect code containing a Preparata code, form a linear Steiner triple system and, respectively, a linear Steiner quadruple system.

The conjecture is based on the common structure of the two known perfect codes containing Preparata codes. The paper does not establish it in general.

333772.title: Győri–Katona–Lemons conjecture for Berge paths in uniform hypergraphs
333772.literal_statement:
Let $r$ and $k$ satisfy $k=r+1>2$, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph, meaning that every hyperedge has size $r$. A **Berge path of length $k$** consists of $k$ distinct hyperedges $e_1,\dots,e_k$ and $k+1$ distinct vertices $v_1,\dots,v_{k+1}$ such that $v_i,v_{i+1}\in e_i$ for each $1\leq i\leq k$. Write $e(\mathcal{H})=|E(\mathcal{H})|$ and $n=n(\mathcal{H})=|V(\mathcal{H})|$. **Győri–Katona–Lemons conjecture.** If $\mathcal{H}$ contains no Berge path of length $k$, then

$$
e(\mathcal{H})\leq \frac{n}{k}\binom{k}{r}=n.
$$

This conjecture is the remaining case of the Győri–Katona–Lemons extension of the Erdős–Gallai theorem for uniform hypergraphs; the paper settles it by proving that an $r$-uniform hypergraph with more than $n$ edges contains a Berge path of length $r+1$.

334190.title: The classification conjecture for extremal 2-increasing sequences
334190.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a 2-increasing sequence in $[r]\times[s]\times[t]$.

**Classification conjecture for extremal 2-increasing sequences.**

$$
|T|\le (rst)^{1/2},
$$

and equality holds if and only if $T$ can be built as follows: choose a coordinate, partition the product of the other two coordinate sets into interval rectangles $R_i\times S_i$ ordered in a 1-increasing fashion, partition the chosen coordinate set into increasing disjoint intervals $T_i$ with $|R_i||S_i|$ proportional to $|T_i|$, place extremal examples in each $R_i\times S_i\times T_i$, and allow permutations of rows, columns, or labels whenever they preserve the 2-increasing property with a different order.

This is a proposed classification of all equality cases, strengthening the preceding decomposition conjecture. The paper says it has survived small-scale searches for counterexamples, but supplies no proof.

343209.title: The positive-density patterns conjecture for affine buildings
343209.literal_statement:
Let $\Delta$ be an irreducible affine building with uniform thickness $2\leq q<\infty$. Let $X\subseteq V_P$ have positive upper density $d^*(X)>0$. For each $k>0$, there exists $K=K(X,k)>0$ such that whenever

$$
\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k\in Q\cap P^+
$$

satisfy $\lambda_k\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_2\geq\lambda_1\geq K\rho$, there exists a subset $\{v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_k\}\subseteq X$ such that

$$
\boldsymbol{d}(v_0,v_j)=\lambda_j\quad\text{for all }1\leq j\leq k
$$

and

$$
\boldsymbol{d}(o,v_0)=\boldsymbol{d}(o,v_1)=\cdots=\boldsymbol{d}(o,v_k).
$$

**Positive-density patterns conjecture.** Every positive-density subset of the vertex set of an irreducible affine building contains these arbitrarily large prescribed configurations with pairwise vector distances from one distinguished vertex and all vertices lying at the same distance from the base vertex. The preceding theorem establishes the analogous result for $(-1)$-type affine buildings, while the remark explains that its current formulation fails for non-$(-1)$-type buildings; the conjecture proposes that the stated formulation remains valid when the prescribed distances lie in $Q\cap P^+$.

344030.title: The threshold-exponent conjecture for K_d-completion
344030.literal_statement:
Consider the $K_d$-completion dynamics on $[n]$, in which copies of $K_d$ missing one edge are iteratively completed, with initial graph $G_0$ having edges $i\leftrightarrow j$ whenever $|i-j|\le d-2$. Let $p_c$ denote the critical probability for saturation. **$K_d$-completion threshold-exponent conjecture.** There exists a power $\gamma=\gamma(d)>0$ such that, for large $n$, $p_c$ lies between two constant multiples of

$$
(\log\log n)^{\gamma}(\log n)^{-1/(d-1)}.
$$

This predicts the threshold scale for nucleation and saturation in the $K_d$-completion dynamics; the paper presents the claim as an unresolved conjecture motivated by simulations and known results for the unpolluted process.

351992.title: Petrova–Shur's conjecture on the Abelian repetition threshold
351992.literal_statement:
For a finite alphabet of size $k$, let ${\sf ART}(k)$ be the infimum of the real numbers $\alpha$ for which there exists an infinite $k$-ary Abelian $\alpha$-power-free word. The paper studies these languages using randomized depth-first searches in their prefix trees.

**Petrova–Shur's conjecture.** The Abelian repetition thresholds satisfy

$$
{\sf ART}(2)>\frac{11}{3};\qquad 2<{\sf ART}(3)\le \frac{5}{2};\qquad {\sf ART}(4)>\frac{9}{5};\qquad {\sf ART}(5)=\frac{3}{2};
$$

$$
\frac{4}{3}<{sf ART}(6)<\frac{3}{2};\qquad {\sf ART}(k)=\frac{k-3}{k-4}\quad\text{for }k\ge 7.
$$

These claims are based on experimental random walks and are intended to describe the observed finiteness or infiniteness of Abelian power-free languages. The authors prove the conjectured inequalities for $k=6,7,8,9,10$; the remaining assertions are experimental conjectures in the paper.

360708.title: The density threshold conjecture for unrestricted sumsets
360708.literal_statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{N}$, and let $\overline{\mathsf d}(A)$ and $\underline{\mathsf d}(A)$ denote its upper and lower densities.

**Density threshold conjecture.** The following assertions hold:

1. If $\overline{\mathsf d}(A)>2/3$, then there is an infinite set $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B\subset A$.
2. If $\underline{\mathsf d}(A)>1/2$, then there is an infinite set $B\subset\mathbb{N}$ such that $B+B\subset A$.

Examples in the paper have upper density arbitrarily close to $2/3$ and lower density arbitrarily close to $1/2$ while avoiding such configurations, motivating the proposed sharp thresholds.

368585.title: Talagrand's bounded-uniformity fractional expectation threshold conjecture
368585.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a finite set, let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $k\leq\log_L|X|$, and let $g\colon{\mleft(\kern-.1em\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{X}{k}\kern-.1em\mright)}\to[0,1]$. Define $\left<g\right>$ by

$$
\left<g\right>:=\left\{S\in 2^X\mathrel{\left|}\sum_{T\subseteq S}g(T)\geq 1\right.\right\},
$$

and for a family $G\subseteq 2^X$ define $w(G,p):=\sum_{S\in G}p^{|S|}$, with $w(g,p)$ defined analogously. **The bounded-uniformity conjecture.** There exists a fixed $L>1$ such that, for all finite sets $X$, all such $k$, all such functions $g$, and all $p\in[0,1]$, if $w(g,p)=1$, then there exists a set $G\subseteq2^X\setminus\{\emptyset\}$ such that $\left<g\right>\subseteq\left<G\right>$ and

$$
w\left(G,\frac{p}{L}\right)\leq1.
$$

This is a restricted form of Talagrand's conjecture whose resolution would imply the full conjecture. Results cited in the source cover constant-size support, and current quantitative bounds do not establish this claim in general.

369863.title: The sparse-graph reformulation of the fractional expectation threshold conjecture
369863.literal_statement:
For $q\in[0,1]$, call a graph $J$ **$q$-sparse** if

$$
\mathbb{E}_qX_I\geq 1\quad\forall I\subseteq J,
$$

where $\mathbb{E}_qX_I$ is the expected number of copies of $I$ in $G_{n,q}$. **Sparse-graph reformulation.** There is a fixed $K$ such that if $H$ is $q$-sparse and $p=Kq$, then

$$
N(H,F)<\mathbb{E}_pX_F\quad\forall F\subset H.
$$

This is stated as an appealing restatement of the fractional expectation threshold conjecture, with the harmless convention change from threshold $1/2$ to $1$ noted in the source. It is therefore open together with that conjecture.

375351.title: Moss–Pedersen conjecture on balanced subfamilies of maximum complement-free families
375351.literal:
Let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. A family $\mathcal F\subseteq\binom{[2n]}{n}$ is **balanced** if every element of $[2n]$ belongs to the same number of members of $\mathcal F$; a balanced subfamily of size $2$ is a complementary pair. 

**Moss–Pedersen conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, there exists a family $\mathcal F\subseteq\binom{[2n]}{n}$ such that

$$
|\mathcal F|=\frac{1}{2}\binom{2n}{n},
$$

$\mathcal F$ contains no balanced subfamily of size $2,4,\ldots,2k$, and $\mathcal F$ contains a balanced subfamily of size $2k+2$.

The first condition makes $\mathcal F$ as large as possible among families containing no complementary pair. The paper’s abstract states that the result is proved constructively, so the conjecture is resolved by the work presented here.

369089.title: Itai–Zehavi conjecture on independent spanning trees
369089.literal: Let $d\geq 1$, let $G$ be a $d$-vertex-connected graph, and let $r$ be a vertex of $G$. A family of spanning trees $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ is said to provide independent paths from $r$ if, for every vertex $v\in V(G)\setminus\\{r\\}$, the paths from $v$ to $r$ in the trees are pairwise internally vertex-disjoint. **Itai–Zehavi conjecture.** For every such $G$ and $r$, there exists a family of $d$ spanning trees $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ providing independent paths from $r$. This conjecture asks for a global strengthening of Menger's theorem, replacing separately chosen disjoint paths by paths organized into spanning trees. The paper proves the conjecture asymptotically with high probability for suitable Erdős–Rényi and random regular graphs, while the general deterministic statement remains open.

371348.title: Kierstead-Kostochka Ore-type analogue of the Chen-Lih-Wu Conjecture
371348.literal:
Let an **equitable $k$-coloring** be a proper $k$-coloring whose color classes have sizes differing by at most one, and let $d(x)$ denote the degree of a vertex $x$. **Kierstead-Kostochka conjecture.** For $k≥3$, if $G$ is a graph satisfying $d(x)+d(y)≤2k$ for every edge $xy$, and $G$ has no equitable $k$-coloring, then $G$ contains either $K_{k+1}$ or $K_{m,2k-m}$ for some odd $m$.

This is the Ore-type analogue of the Chen-Lih-Wu Conjecture. The paper proves it when $k$ is at least a fixed positive proportion of the number of vertices, while the case $k=o(n)$ remains a stated direction for future work.

371577.title: Path-graph incompatibility robustness conjecture
371577.literal:
Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, and let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices. The incompatibility robustness of a graph is denoted by $\eta(\cdot)$.

**Path-graph robustness conjecture.** For all $n\geq 1$,

$$
\eta(P_{2n})=\eta(P_{2n+1})=\eta(C_{2n+2})=\frac{2}{2n+2}\csc\Big(\frac{\pi}{2n+2}\Big).
$$

The prediction is motivated by comparisons with exact values obtained by semidefinite programming and by the asymptotically tight bounds previously established for paths. It remains open whether these equalities hold for every $n\geq 1$.

363627.title: Lehel's approximate conjecture for uniform tight cycles
363627.literal:
For $k\geq3$, let a $k$-uniform tight cycle be a cyclic sequence of vertices whose edges are the sets of $k$ consecutive vertices. Consider a red-blue edge-colouring of the complete $k$-graph on $n$ vertices.

364140.title: The dimension conjecture for the product-measure locus in the permutation simplex
364140.literal:
Let $S_m$ be the symmetric group, let $\Delta(S_m)$ be the simplex of probability distributions on $S_m$, and let $P_m\subseteq\Delta(S_m)$ be the locus hit by product measures. A **pure cycle** is a permutation with exactly one nontrivial cycle and all other points fixed. Write

$$
C(m)=\sum_{k=2}^m \frac{m!}{k\cdot (m-k)!}
$$

for the number of pure cycles in $S_m$.

**Dimension conjecture.** For all $m$, the dimension of $P_m$ is exactly $C(m)$.

The paper proves the upper bound $\dim P_m\leq C(m)$ and verifies equality for $m\leq 7$, but the equality is conjectural for general $m$.

364945.title: Ge–Xu–Zhang conjecture for clique odd-colourings
364945.literal:
For a graph $H$, let $r_H(n)$ be the least number of colours in an edge-colouring of $K_n$ with no even-chromatic copy of $H$. For a clique $K_t$, having an even number of edges is equivalent to $t\equiv 0,1\pmod 4$.

**Ge–Xu–Zhang conjecture.** For every positive integer $t\geq 4$ with $t\equiv 0,1\pmod 4$,

$$
r_{K_t}(n)=n^{o(1)}.

364946.title: The clique conjecture for unique-chromatic colourings
364946.literal:
Given an edge-colouring of $K_n$, a copy of $H$ is **unique-chromatic** if some colour occupies exactly one edge of it. An edge-colouring is $H$-unique if every copy of $H$ is unique-chromatic, and $u_H(n)$ is the least number of colours in an $H$-unique edge-colouring of $K_n$.

**Clique uniqueness conjecture.** For every positive integer $t\geq 2$,

$$
u_{K_t}(n)=n^{o(1)}.
$$

The paper proves a polynomial lower bound for every non-complete graph without isolated vertices, so cliques are conjectured to be precisely the graphs admitting sub-polynomially many colours. The cases $t=4$ and $t=5$ are proved; the remaining clique cases are open.

357323.title: Polynomial chromatic-number conjecture for high-girth intersection graphs of lines
357323.literal: Let $g\in\mathbb{N}$. An intersection graph of lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$ has one vertex for each line and edges joining intersecting lines; its girth is the length of its shortest cycle. **Polynomial chromatic-number conjecture for high-girth line graphs.** For every $g\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every sufficiently large $n$, there exists an intersection graph of $n$ lines in $\mathbb{R}^3$ of girth at least $g$ and chromatic number at least $n^{\varepsilon}$. 358528.title: Sublogarithmic out-neighbourhood chromatic conjecture
358528.literal:
Let $G$ be an $N$-vertex graph and $T$ a tournament on the same vertex set. For a vertex $v$, write $N_T^+(v)$ for its out-neighbourhood in $T$.

**Sublogarithmic out-neighbourhood conjecture.** There exists a function $f(N)$ satisfying

$$
f(N)=o(\log N)
$$

such that, for every $N$-vertex graph $G$ with $\chi(G)\geqslant f(N)$ and every tournament $T$ on the same vertex set, there is a vertex $v$ for which

$$
\chi(G[N_T^+(v)])\geqslant 3.
$$

This asks whether a chromatic-number threshold growing strictly slower than $\log N$ suffices to force a non-bipartite out-neighbourhood; the source leaves it open.

360248.title: The good ordering conjecture for tournament twin-width and clique number
360248.literal:
For a tournament $T$ and an ordering $\prec$ of $V(T)$, let $T^{\prec}$ be its backedge graph. A **BST-ordering** is the ordering associated with a binary search tree satisfying the tournament-neighbourhood conditions described in the paper. **The good ordering conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that, for every tournament $T$, there exists an ordering $\prec^*$ of $V(T)$ such that

$$
\omega(T^{\prec^*})\leq f(\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(T))\quad\text{and}\quad tww(T,\prec^*)\leq f(tww(T)).
$$

If true, this would imply the bounded twin-width conjecture; the paper notes that BST-orderings are natural candidates because they already provide the required twin-width bound, leaving the backedge-graph clique bound open.

361174.title: Bounded-region realization conjecture for hyperplane arrangements
361174.literal:
Fix integers $m\geq4$ and $n\geq m$. Consider the $m-1$ coordinate hyperplanes in $\mathbb R^{m-1}$ and add $n$ further hyperplanes. **Bounded-region realization conjecture.** For every integer $k$ satisfying

$$
1\leq k\leq\binom{n+m-2}{m-1},
$$

there exist $n$ hyperplanes such that the arrangement of all $m+n-1$ hyperplanes has exactly $k$ bounded regions. The preceding argument establishes the asserted realization for sufficiently large parameters, while the stated uniform range for all $m\geq4$ and $n\geq m$ remains the conjectural part.

354067.title: The b-conjecture for connected Jack coefficients
354067.literal:
Let $d^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ be defined by

$$
\log\left(\tau_b(t,\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q},\mathbf{r})\right)=\sum_{n\geq1}\sum_{\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n}t^n \frac{d^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}}{z_\lambda(1+b)^{\ell(\lambda)}}p_\lambda q_\mu r_\nu.
$$

The coefficients $h^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ are related to them by

$$
h^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}=\frac{n d^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}}{z_\lambda(1+b)^{\ell(\lambda)-1}}.
$$

**b-conjecture.** For all partitions $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n\geq 1$, the coefficient $h^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ is a polynomial in $b$ with non-negative integer coefficients. The $b$-conjecture is a connected analogue of the Matching-Jack conjecture and concerns the integrality and positivity of the associated coefficients.

354147.title: Pósa-type degree-sequence conjecture for monochromatic cycle partitions
354147.literal:
Let $d_1\leq\dots\leq d_n$ be the degree sequence of a graph $G$. **The degree-sequence conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that, for every $\beta>0$, every integer $r\geq 2$, and all sufficiently large $n$, if

$$
d_i\geq i+\beta n
$$

for every $i\leq n/2$, then every $r$-edge-colouring of $G$ admits a partition of $V(G)$ into at most $f(r)$ monochromatic cycles. This conjecture extends Pósa-type Hamiltonicity conditions to coloured cycle partitions; an approximate solution is known for $r=2$, but the general assertion remains open.

356297.title: The logarithmic-length conjecture for binary words with a prescribed number of subsequences
356297.literal:
A **binary word** is a finite word over the alphabet $\{\mathsf{A},\mathsf{B}\}$. For a binary word $\mathfrak{w}$, let $\mathsf{P}(\mathfrak{w})$ denote its number of nonempty subsequences.

**Logarithmic-length conjecture.** For every integer $n\geqslant 1$, there exists a binary word $\mathfrak{w}$ such that

$$
|\mathfrak{w}|=O(\log n)
$$

and

$$
\mathsf{P}(\mathfrak{w})=n.
$$

The Fibonacci-type alternating words show that any binary word with exactly $n$ subsequences must have length $\Omega(\log n)$, so the conjecture asks whether this lower bound is sharp up to a constant factor. The source does not provide a resolution.

349872.title: Large expander conjecture for high-genus triangulations
349872.literal:
Let $g_n$ satisfy

$$
\frac{g_n}{n}\to\theta\in(0,1/2),
$$

and let $\mathbf{T_{n,g_n}}$ be a uniform triangulation of genus $g_n$ with $3n$ edges. An induced subgraph is a **$\kappa$-expander** if every set of vertices has at least $\kappa$ times its size in edges leaving it. **Large expander conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a $\kappa>0$ depending only on $\varepsilon$ and $\theta$ such that, with high probability, $\mathbf{T_{n,g_n}}$ contains an induced subgraph $G_n$ with at least $(1-\varepsilon)3n$ edges that is a $\kappa$-expander. This conjecture extends the paper's theorem for uniform unicellular maps to uniform triangulations, and concerns the global geometric structure of high-genus maps. It is presented as an ambitious open problem.

322967.title: The odd Goldbach conjecture
322967.literal_statement: Let $x$ be an odd integer larger than $1$. **Odd Goldbach conjecture.** Every odd number $x$ larger than $1$ can be expressed as the sum of at most three primes. This is a classical open problem in additive number theory. It is also commonly formulated, in an almost equivalent and slightly stronger form, by asserting that every odd number greater than seven is the sum of three odd primes; the paper proves the weaker bound of five primes.

324165.title: A minor characterization of signed graphs with signed Colin de Verdière parameter at most three
324165.literal_statement:
A **signed graph** is a pair $(G,\Sigma)$ consisting of a graph $G$ and a set $\Sigma$ of odd edges. Let $\nu(G,\Sigma)$ denote its signed Colin de Verdière parameter. Write $K_5^o$ for the signed complete graph on five vertices with the specified odd-edge pattern, and $K_4^=$ for the corresponding signed complete graph on four vertices. A **$\Delta Y$-transformation** replaces a triangle by a new degree-three vertex adjacent to its vertices, and a **$Y\Delta$-transformation** is the reverse operation. 

**Minor characterization conjecture.** A signed graph $(G,\Sigma)$ has $\nu(G,\Sigma)\leq 3$ if and only if $(G,\Sigma)$ has no minor isomorphic to $K_5^o$, $K_4^=$, or any signed graph $(H,\Omega)$ that can be obtained from $K_4^=$ by a sequence of $\Delta Y$- and $Y\Delta$-transformations.

This conjecture seeks the next excluded-minor characterization for the signed Colin de Verdière parameter after the established characterization for parameter at most two. The paper notes that $\nu(K_5^o)=4$ and $\nu(K_4^=)=4$, and that the parameter remains four under the indicated transformations; the proposed characterization is otherwise unresolved in the supplied text.

326378.title: Indexed strong Goldbach representation conjecture
326378.literal_statement:
Distribute the positive integers into three columns $C_1$, $C_2$ and $C_3$ by residue class modulo $3$, and let $t_n^\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^*$ denote the integer in column $C_n$ and row $\alpha$. Let $\mathbb{P}$ be the set of positive prime numbers, ordered as $p_1=2,p_2=3,p_3=5,\dots$, and let $p_m^\delta$ denote the prime in the $m$-th prime column and row $\delta$. For a positive even integer $t_n^\alpha$, the conjecture specifies a representation using one prime in the corresponding prime column and another prime.

**Indexed strong Goldbach representation conjecture.** Let $t_n^\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^*$ be a positive even integer. Then there esist two prime numbers $p_{n}^{\delta(\alpha)}, \,p_{m}^{\gamma}\in\mathbb{P}$ such that

$$
t_{n}^{\alpha}=p_{n}^{\delta(\alpha)}+p_{m}^{\gamma}.
$$

This is presented as a reformulation of the strong Goldbach conjecture in the paper's column-and-row notation. Its status therefore tracks the unresolved strong Goldbach problem rather than constituting an independent result.

332014.title: The weight-support system conjecture for perfect codes containing Preparata codes
332014.literal_statement:
Let $C$ be a binary perfect code containing a Preparata code. For an extended perfect code, consider the codewords of weight $4$; for a non-extended perfect code, consider the codewords of weight $3$. Their supports form the corresponding Steiner system. A system is **linear** when it is equivalent to the system formed by the supports of the weight-$3$ words of the linear Hamming code.

**Weight-support system conjecture.** All codewords of weight $3$ of a perfect code containing a Preparata code, and all codewords of weight $4$ of an extended perfect code containing a Preparata code, form a linear Steiner triple system and, respectively, a linear Steiner quadruple system.

The conjecture is based on the common structure of the two known perfect codes containing Preparata codes. The paper does not establish it in general.

333772.title: Győri–Katona–Lemons conjecture for Berge paths in uniform hypergraphs
333772.literal_statement:
Let $r$ and $k$ satisfy $k=r+1>2$, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph, meaning that every hyperedge has size $r$. A **Berge path of length $k$** consists of $k$ distinct hyperedges $e_1,\dots,e_k$ and $k+1$ distinct vertices $v_1,\dots,v_{k+1}$ such that $v_i,v_{i+1}\in e_i$ for each $1\leq i\leq k$. Write $e(\mathcal{H})=|E(\mathcal{H})|$ and $n=n(\mathcal{H})=|V(\mathcal{H})|$. **Győri–Katona–Lemons conjecture.** If $\mathcal{H}$ contains no Berge path of length $k$, then

$$
e(\mathcal{H})\leq \frac{n}{k}\binom{k}{r}=n.
$$

This conjecture is the remaining case of the Győri–Katona–Lemons extension of the Erdős–Gallai theorem for uniform hypergraphs; the paper settles it by proving that an $r$-uniform hypergraph with more than $n$ edges contains a Berge path of length $r+1$.

334190.title: The classification conjecture for extremal 2-increasing sequences
334190.literal_statement:
Let $T$ be a 2-increasing sequence in $[r]\times[s]\times[t]$.

**Classification conjecture for extremal 2-increasing sequences.**

$$
|T|\le (rst)^{1/2},
$$

and equality holds if and only if $T$ can be built as follows: choose a coordinate, partition the product of the other two coordinate sets into interval rectangles $R_i\times S_i$ ordered in a 1-increasing fashion, partition the chosen coordinate set into increasing disjoint intervals $T_i$ with $|R_i||S_i|$ proportional to $|T_i|$, place extremal examples in each $R_i\times S_i\times T_i$, and allow permutations of rows, columns, or labels whenever they preserve the 2-increasing property with a different order.

This is a proposed classification of all equality cases, strengthening the preceding decomposition conjecture. The paper says it has survived small-scale searches for counterexamples, but supplies no proof.

343209.title: The positive-density patterns conjecture for affine buildings
343209.literal_statement:
Let $\Delta$ be an irreducible affine building with uniform thickness $2\leq q<\infty$. Let $X\subseteq V_P$ have positive upper density $d^*(X)>0$. For each $k>0$, there exists $K=K(X,k)>0$ such that whenever

$$
\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k\in Q\cap P^+
$$

satisfy $\lambda_k\geq\cdots\geq\lambda_2\geq\lambda_1\geq K\rho$, there exists a subset $\{v_0,v_1,\ldots,v_k\}\subseteq X$ such that

$$
\boldsymbol{d}(v_0,v_j)=\lambda_j\quad\text{for all }1\leq j\leq k
$$

and

$$
\boldsymbol{d}(o,v_0)=\boldsymbol{d}(o,v_1)=\cdots=\boldsymbol{d}(o,v_k).
$$

**Positive-density patterns conjecture.** Every positive-density subset of the vertex set of an irreducible affine building contains these arbitrarily large prescribed configurations with pairwise vector distances from one distinguished vertex and all vertices lying at the same distance from the base vertex. The preceding theorem establishes the analogous result for $(-1)$-type affine buildings, while the remark explains that its current formulation fails for non-$(-1)$-type buildings; the conjecture proposes that the stated formulation remains valid when the prescribed distances lie in $Q\cap P^+$.

344030.title: The threshold-exponent conjecture for K_d-completion
344030.literal_statement:
Consider the $K_d$-completion dynamics on $[n]$, in which copies of $K_d$ missing one edge are iteratively completed, with initial graph $G_0$ having edges $i\leftrightarrow j$ whenever $|i-j|\le d-2$. Let $p_c$ denote the critical probability for saturation. **$K_d$-completion threshold-exponent conjecture.** There exists a power $\gamma=\gamma(d)>0$ such that, for large $n$, $p_c$ lies between two constant multiples of

$$
(\log\log n)^{\gamma}(\log n)^{-1/(d-1)}.
$$

This predicts the threshold scale for nucleation and saturation in the $K_d$-completion dynamics; the paper presents the claim as an unresolved conjecture motivated by simulations and known results for the unpolluted process.

351992.title: Petrova–Shur's conjecture on the Abelian repetition threshold
351992.literal_statement:
For a finite alphabet of size $k$, let ${\sf ART}(k)$ be the infimum of the real numbers $\alpha$ for which there exists an infinite $k$-ary Abelian $\alpha$-power-free word. The paper studies these languages using randomized depth-first searches in their prefix trees.

**Petrova–Shur's conjecture.** The Abelian repetition thresholds satisfy

$$
{\sf ART}(2)>\frac{11}{3};\qquad 2<{\sf ART}(3)\le \frac{5}{2};\qquad {\sf ART}(4)>\frac{9}{5};\qquad {\sf ART}(5)=\frac{3}{2};
$$

$$
\frac{4}{3}<{sf ART}(6)<\frac{3}{2};\qquad {\sf ART}(k)=\frac{k-3}{k-4}\quad\text{for }k\ge 7.
$$

These claims are based on experimental random walks and are intended to describe the observed finiteness or infiniteness of Abelian power-free languages. The authors prove the conjectured inequalities for $k=6,7,8,9,10$; the remaining assertions are experimental conjectures in the paper.

368585.title: Talagrand's bounded-uniformity fractional expectation threshold conjecture
368585.literal_statement:
Let $X$ be a finite set, let $k\in\mathbb{N}$ satisfy $k\leq\log_L|X|$, and let $g\colon{\mleft(\kern-.1em\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{X}{k}\kern-.1em\mright)}\to[0,1]$. Define $\left<g\right>$ by

$$
\left<g\right>:=\left\{S\in 2^X\mathrel{\left|}\sum_{T\subseteq S}g(T)\geq 1\right.\right\},
$$

and for a family $G\subseteq 2^X$ define $w(G,p):=\sum_{S\in G}p^{|S|}$, with $w(g,p)$ defined analogously. **The bounded-uniformity conjecture.** There exists a fixed $L>1$ such that, for all finite sets $X$, all such $k$, all such functions $g$, and all $p\in[0,1]$, if $w(g,p)=1$, then there exists a set $G\subseteq2^X\setminus\{\emptyset\}$ such that $\left<g\right>\subseteq\left<G\right>$ and

$$
w\left(G,\frac{p}{L}\right)\leq1.
$$

This is a restricted form of Talagrand's conjecture whose resolution would imply the full conjecture. Results cited in the source cover constant-size support, and current quantitative bounds do not establish this claim in general.

369863.title: The sparse-graph reformulation of the fractional expectation threshold conjecture
369863.literal_statement:
For $q\in[0,1]$, call a graph $J$ **$q$-sparse** if

$$
\mathbb{E}_qX_I\geq 1\quad\forall I\subseteq J,
$$

where $\mathbb{E}_qX_I$ is the expected number of copies of $I$ in $G_{n,q}$. **Sparse-graph reformulation.** There is a fixed $K$ such that if $H$ is $q$-sparse and $p=Kq$, then

$$
N(H,F)<\mathbb{E}_pX_F\quad\forall F\subset H.
$$

This is stated as an appealing restatement of the fractional expectation threshold conjecture, with the harmless convention change from threshold $1/2$ to $1$ noted in the source. It is therefore open together with that conjecture.

375351.title: Moss–Pedersen conjecture on balanced subfamilies of maximum complement-free families
375351.literal:
Let $k\geq 1$ be an integer. A family $\mathcal F\subseteq\binom{[2n]}{n}$ is **balanced** if every element of $[2n]$ belongs to the same number of members of $\mathcal F$; a balanced subfamily of size $2$ is a complementary pair. 

**Moss–Pedersen conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$, there exists a family $\mathcal F\subseteq\binom{[2n]}{n}$ such that

$$
|\mathcal F|=\frac{1}{2}\binom{2n}{n},
$$

$\mathcal F$ contains no balanced subfamily of size $2,4,\ldots,2k$, and $\mathcal F$ contains a balanced subfamily of size $2k+2$.

The first condition makes $\mathcal F$ as large as possible among families containing no complementary pair. The paper’s abstract states that the result is proved constructively, so the conjecture is resolved by the work presented here.

369089.title: Itai–Zehavi conjecture on independent spanning trees
369089.literal: Let $d\geq 1$, let $G$ be a $d$-vertex-connected graph, and let $r$ be a vertex of $G$. A family of spanning trees $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ is said to provide independent paths from $r$ if, for every vertex $v\in V(G)\setminus\\{r\\}$, the paths from $v$ to $r$ in the trees are pairwise internally vertex-disjoint. **Itai–Zehavi conjecture.** For every such $G$ and $r$, there exists a family of $d$ spanning trees $T_1,\ldots,T_d$ providing independent paths from $r$. This conjecture asks for a global strengthening of Menger's theorem, replacing separately chosen disjoint paths by paths organized into spanning trees. The paper proves the conjecture asymptotically with high probability for suitable Erdős–Rényi and random regular graphs, while the general deterministic statement remains open.

371348.title: Kierstead-Kostochka Ore-type analogue of the Chen-Lih-Wu Conjecture
371348.literal:
Let an **equitable $k$-coloring** be a proper $k$-coloring whose color classes have sizes differing by at most one, and let $d(x)$ denote the degree of a vertex $x$. **Kierstead-Kostochka conjecture.** For $k≥3$, if $G$ is a graph satisfying $d(x)+d(y)≤2k$ for every edge $xy$, and $G$ has no equitable $k$-coloring, then $G$ contains either $K_{k+1}$ or $K_{m,2k-m}$ for some odd $m$.

This is the Ore-type analogue of the Chen-Lih-Wu Conjecture. The paper proves it when $k$ is at least a fixed positive proportion of the number of vertices, while the case $k=o(n)$ remains a stated direction for future work.

371577.title: Path-graph incompatibility robustness conjecture
371577.literal:
Let $P_n$ be the path graph on $n$ vertices, and let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices. The incompatibility robustness of a graph is denoted by $\eta(\cdot)$.

**Path-graph robustness conjecture.** For all $n\geq 1$,

$$
\eta(P_{2n})=\eta(P_{2n+1})=\eta(C_{2n+2})=\frac{2}{2n+2}\csc\Big(\frac{\pi}{2n+2}\Big).
$$

The prediction is motivated by comparisons with exact values obtained by semidefinite programming and by the asymptotically tight bounds previously established for paths. It remains open whether these equalities hold for every $n\geq 1$.

363627.title: Lehel's approximate conjecture for uniform tight cycles
363627.literal:
For $k\geq3$, let a $k$-uniform tight cycle be a cyclic sequence of vertices whose edges are the sets of $k$ consecutive vertices. Consider a red-blue edge-colouring of the complete $k$-graph on $n$ vertices.

**Approximate Lehel conjecture.** There exist constants $c_k\geq1$ and $n_0(k)\in\mathbb N$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0(k)$, the coloured complete $k$-graph contains vertex-disjoint red and blue tight cycles whose union contains at least $n-c_k$ vertices.

The paper proves the weaker bound $n-o(n)$ and notes that the error cannot be zero. A constant error is known for $k=3$, while the conjecture remains open for every $k\geq4$.

364140.title: The dimension conjecture for the product-measure locus in the permutation simplex
364140.literal:
Let $S_m$ be the symmetric group, let $\Delta(S_m)$ be the simplex of probability distributions on $S_m$, and let $P_m\subseteq\Delta(S_m)$ be the locus hit by product measures. A **pure cycle** is a permutation with exactly one nontrivial cycle and all other points fixed. Write

$$
C(m)=\sum_{k=2}^m \frac{m!}{k\cdot (m-k)!}
$$

for the number of pure cycles in $S_m$.

**Dimension conjecture.** For all $m$, the dimension of $P_m$ is exactly $C(m)$.

The paper proves the upper bound $\dim P_m\leq C(m)$ and verifies equality for $m\leq 7$, but the equality is conjectural for general $m$.

364945.title: Ge–Xu–Zhang conjecture for clique odd-colourings
364945.literal:
For a graph $H$, let $r_H(n)$ be the least number of colours in an edge-colouring of $K_n$ with no even-chromatic copy of $H$. For a clique $K_t$, having an even number of edges is equivalent to $t\equiv 0,1\pmod 4$.

**Ge–Xu–Zhang conjecture.** For every positive integer $t\geq 4$ with $t\equiv 0,1\pmod 4$,

$$
r_{K_t}(n)=n^{o(1)}.
$$

For these values of $t$, $K_t$ is not even-decomposable, so this is the clique case predicted by Versteegen's conjecture. The cases $t=4$ and $t=5$ are established in the paper, while the general statement remains open.

364946.title: The clique conjecture for unique-chromatic colourings
364946.literal:
Given an edge-colouring of $K_n$, a copy of $H$ is **unique-chromatic** if some colour occupies exactly one edge of it. An edge-colouring is $H$-unique if every copy of $H$ is unique-chromatic, and $u_H(n)$ is the least number of colours in an $H$-unique edge-colouring of $K_n$.

**Clique uniqueness conjecture.** For every positive integer $t\geq 2$,

$$
u_{K_t}(n)=n^{o(1)}.
$$

The paper proves a polynomial lower bound for every non-complete graph without isolated vertices, so cliques are conjectured to be precisely the graphs admitting sub-polynomially many colours. The cases $t=4$ and $t=5$ are proved; the remaining clique cases are open.

357323.title: Polynomial chromatic-number conjecture for high-girth intersection graphs of lines
357323.literal: Let $g\in\mathbb{N}$. 358528.title: Sublogarithmic out-neighbourhood chromatic conjecture
358528.literal:
Let $G$ be an $N$-vertex graph and $T$ a tournament on the same vertex set. For a vertex $v$, write $N_T^+(v)$ for its out-neighbourhood in $T$.

**Sublogarithmic out-neighbourhood conjecture.** There exists a function $f(N)$ satisfying

$$
f(N)=o(\log N)
$$

such that, for every $N$-vertex graph $G$ with $\chi(G)\geqslant f(N)$ and every tournament $T$ on the same vertex set, there is a vertex $v$ for which

$$
\chi(G[N_T^+(v)])\geqslant 3.
$$

This asks whether a chromatic-number threshold growing strictly slower than $\log N$ suffices to force a non-bipartite out-neighbourhood; the source leaves it open.

360248.title: The good ordering conjecture for tournament twin-width and clique number
360248.literal:
For a tournament $T$ and an ordering $\prec$ of $V(T)$, let $T^{\prec}$ be its backedge graph. A **BST-ordering** is the ordering associated with a binary search tree satisfying the tournament-neighbourhood conditions described in the paper. **The good ordering conjecture.** There exists a function $f$ such that, for every tournament $T$, there exists an ordering $\prec^*$ of $V(T)$ such that

$$
\omega(T^{\prec^*})\leq f(\operatorname{\overrightarrow{\omega}}(T))\quad\text{and}\quad tww(T,\prec^*)\leq f(tww(T)).
$$

If true, this would imply the bounded twin-width conjecture; the paper notes that BST-orderings are natural candidates because they already provide the required twin-width bound, leaving the backedge-graph clique bound open.

354067.title: The b-conjecture for connected Jack coefficients
354067.literal:
Let $d^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ be defined by

$$
\log\left(\tau_b(t,\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q},\mathbf{r})\right)=\sum_{n\geq1}\sum_{\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n}t^n \frac{d^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}}{z_\lambda(1+b)^{\ell(\lambda)}}p_\lambda q_\mu r_\nu.
$$

The coefficients $h^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ are related to them by

$$
h^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}=\frac{n d^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}}{z_\lambda(1+b)^{\ell(\lambda)-1}}.
$$

**b-conjecture.** For all partitions $\lambda,\mu,\nu\vdash n\geq 1$, the coefficient $h^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}$ is a polynomial in $b$ with non-negative integer coefficients. The $b$-conjecture is a connected analogue of the Matching-Jack conjecture and concerns the integrality and positivity of the associated coefficients.

354147.title: Pósa-type degree-sequence conjecture for monochromatic cycle partitions
354147.literal:
Let $d_1\leq\dots\leq d_n$ be the degree sequence of a graph $G$. **The degree-sequence conjecture.** There is a function $f$ such that, for every $\beta>0$, every integer $r\geq 2$, and all sufficiently large $n$, if

$$
d_i\geq i+\beta n
$$

for every $i\leq n/2$, then every $r$-edge-colouring of $G$ admits a partition of $V(G)$ into at most $f(r)$ monochromatic cycles. This conjecture extends Pósa-type Hamiltonicity conditions to coloured cycle partitions; an approximate solution is known for $r=2$, but the general assertion remains open.

356297.title: The logarithmic-length conjecture for binary words with a prescribed number of subsequences
356297.literal:
A **binary word** is a finite word over the alphabet $\{\mathsf{A},\mathsf{B}\}$. For a binary word $\mathfrak{w}$, let $\mathsf{P}(\mathfrak{w})$ denote its number of nonempty subsequences.

**Logarithmic-length conjecture.** For every integer $n\geqslant 1$, there exists a binary word $\mathfrak{w}$ such that

$$
|\mathfrak{w}|=O(\log n)
$$

and

$$
\mathsf{P}(\mathfrak{w})=n.
$$

The Fibonacci-type alternating words show that any binary word with exactly $n$ subsequences must have length $\Omega(\log n)$, so the conjecture asks whether this lower bound is sharp up to a constant factor. The source does not provide a resolution.

349872.title: Large expander conjecture for high-genus triangulations
349872.literal:
Let $g_n$ satisfy

$$
\frac{g_n}{n}\to\theta\in(0,1/2),
$$

and let $\mathbf{T_{n,g_n}}$ be a uniform triangulation of genus $g_n$ with $3n$ edges. An induced subgraph is a **$\kappa$-expander** if every set of vertices has at least $\kappa$ times its size in edges leaving it. **Large expander conjecture.** For every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a $\kappa>0$ depending only on $\varepsilon$ and $\theta$ such that, with high probability, $\mathbf{T_{n,g_n}}$ contains an induced subgraph $G_n$ with at least $(1-\varepsilon)3n$ edges that is a $\kappa$-expander. This conjecture extends the paper's theorem for uniform unicellular maps to uniform triangulations, and concerns the global geometric structure of high-genus maps. It is presented as an ambitious open problem.

351449.title: Grytczuk–Kordulewski–Niewiadomski conjecture on extremal square-free words
351449.literal:
A **square-free word** is a finite word over a finite alphabet that contains no factor of the form $XX$ for a nonempty word $X$. An **extremal square-free word** is a square-free word none of whose extensions, obtained by inserting one letter at any position, is square-free.

**Grytczuk–Kordulewski–Niewiadomski conjecture.** There exists no extremal square-free word over a finite alphabet of size at least $4$.

This conjecture concerns the possible existence of extremal square-free words over larger alphabets. Infinitely many ternary extremal square-free words are known, while the conjecture was open for every finite alphabet according to the authors.
